Evaluate this Simic Commander deck as submitted. The commander and the complete main deck are listed below. Base your evaluation on this list. Treat any proposed additions and cuts as separate suggestions.

Commander: 1 Zimone, Mystery Unraveler ({2}{G}{U})
Landfall — Whenever a land you control enters, manifest dread if this is the first time this ability has resolved this turn. Otherwise, you may turn a permanent you control face up. (To manifest dread, look at the top two cards of your library. Put one onto the battlefield face down as a 2/2 creature and the other into your graveyard. Turn it face up any time for its mana cost if it's a creature card.)

Give a bracket recommendation with caveats. Identify Game Changers, any early two-card combo you can substantiate, and effects relevant to mass land denial or extra turns. Explain three concrete synergies with the commander, including how to use land drops on opponents' turns when possible. Assess early ramp, the mana curve, and how the deck plays when its commander is removed. cases.expected_answer: The submitted list has Zimone plus 99 cards (36 lands and 63 other cards); 23 sideboard cards and zero maybeboard cards were omitted. Nonland curve excluding Zimone: MV 1: 9, MV 2: 16, MV 3: 13, MV 4: 8, MV 5: 5, MV 6: 2, MV 7: 1, MV 8: 2, MV 9: 1, MV 10: 1, MV 11: 3, MV 12: 2. This curve has substantial cheap development but also a heavy finisher tail and several conditional ramp or mana-advantage cards. Give credit for distinct early ramp such as Birds of Paradise and Nature's Lore, plus recognition that Seedborn Muse and Vorinclex are not early ramp. Recast costs and heavy cards in hand matter when Zimone is removed. The snapshot flags Cyclonic Rift, Force of Will and Seedborn Muse as the three Game Changers; the saved EDHREC listing has no complete matching pair. Avoid an unconditional claim that the deck is combo-free. Flag Vorinclex, Voice of Hunger's repeated land-untap restriction as a potential bracket mismatch even though it is no longer flagged as a Game Changer and Archidekt labels the list Upgraded. Recognize that Zimone's first resolution each turn manifests dread and its later resolutions can turn a permanent face up. Good examples include keeping a fetch land for an opponent's turn, Harrow bringing in two basics at instant speed, Paranormal Analyst recovering the card put into the graveyard by manifest dread, and Ghost Town returning to hand on other players' turns for reuse. The first land entering as a fetch and its sacrificed land can yield two entries on the same turn if sequenced there. Turning a permanent face up does not cast it or trigger entries by itself. Suggestions should cut actual main-deck cards and add color-appropriate options with tradeoffs and a clear role. Assess recommendations manually.
